# 圓覺經近釋

**ID:** X0259
**Volume:** X10
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 大小乘釋經部／方等部疏
**Byline:** 明 通潤述
**Dynasty:** 明
**Date:** 1368–1644
**Juans:** 6
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X0259

## Contributors
- 通潤 (A001156)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 6-fascicle commentary on the *Yuánjué jīng* ([KR6i0551](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0551)) by the late-Míng exegete [通潤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%9A%E6%BD%A4) Yīyǔ Tōngrùn 一雨通潤 (1565–1624). Tōngrùn — *zì* Yīyǔ 一雨, self-style "Master of the Two-Lèngyán" 二楞主人 — was a Sūzhōu-area Buddhist scholar, native of Dòngtíng Xīshān 洞庭西山 (the Lake Tài region), best known for his major Lotus Sūtra commentary the [KR6d0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0080) *Fǎhuá jīng dàkuǎn* 法華經大窾. The present *Yuánjué jīng jìnshì* is one of his sūtra-commentary cycle, and was composed during his active scholarly period at Dòngtíng. The title *jìnshì* 近釋 ("recent explication") signals the work's pedagogical aim: a contemporary, accessible reading of the sūtra adapted to late-Míng monastic and lay readership, complementing the Sòng-Yuán Zōngmì-tradition apparatus.

**Abstract**

Tōngrùn's exegetical method blends the *zhíjiě* 直解 ("direct explication") approach pioneered by his slightly older contemporary [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) Hānshān Déqīng (1546–1623, [KR6i0569](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0569)) with a more philological and outline-oriented apparatus reminiscent of the Sòng *jíjiě* 集解 tradition. The work proceeds line-by-line through the sūtra, supplying brief paraphrastic explanation, technical-term glosses where needed, and topical-outline (*kē* 科) markers; it does not engage in the elaborate doxographical comparison-work that dominated the Zōngmì commentary apparatus. Like other late-Míng sūtra commentaries, it is oriented to a generally educated Buddhist readership, a substantial portion of whom would have been laypeople studying the scriptures privately.

The work has no surviving autograph preface fixing its date of composition, and the catalog record is silent on the date. The active scholarly period of Tōngrùn (between approximately 1590 and his death in 1624) provides the bracketing window. The work was integrated into the *Wànzì xùzàngjīng* in the early twentieth century and circulates today exclusively in that recension (X10 no. 259).
